transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump is back in Washington D.C. after a four-day trip to Asia.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports on a press conference Trump is planning for Friday to discuss the trip.
U.S. presidents typically hold a news conference at the end of foreign trips
in order to highlight all that happened behind the scenes and explain what was accomplished.
But President Trump left China without meeting with the press.
Now, China has a history of controlling the media, including banning one U.S. reporter this trip
after she shouted a question during the event.
And it wasn't until the flight back and after President Putin held his own press conference
that Trump announced on social media that he would be holding a press conference at the White House.
In addition to discussing the historic trilateral meeting with China and Russia,
Trump says he'll also be discussing trade deals with Thailand and the Philippines.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
U.S. envoy Jared Kushner says he believes Russia is comfortable with NATO-like security guarantees
for a post-war Ukraine.
His remarks Thursday came in Berlin during a meeting of European allies who have expressed concern
about President Trump's meeting in China with Russian leader Vladimir Putin, Europe,
pushing to be included in U.S.-backed talks to end the war.
On the same day that A.I. giant Anthropic posted the biggest initial public offering on record,
four people were arrested for blocking an entrance to Anthropic's San Francisco offices Thursday
from member station KQED in San Francisco, Juan Carlos Laro reports.
As Anthropic made its stock market debut, more than 100 protesters gathered outside
of the company's offices to raise alarms over the risks of rapidly advancing artificial intelligence.
Among those arrested was stop A.I. co-founder Guido Reichstader.
On its website, Anthropic says RSI could increase risks of humans losing control of A.I.
For NPR News, I'm Juan Carlos Laro in San Francisco.
Director of Mercy One, Genesis Community Care in the Quad Cities, he says repeated exposure is the problem.
Right after the detonation, there will be lead dust in the air and you can breathe that in and then that can enter the blood.
The detonation had been planned for Friday. You're listening to NPR News.
The Senate has passed a bipartisan bill aimed at speeding up the permitting process for the construction of new power plants,
transmission lines, and other energy infrastructure in a bid to meet demand and lower electricity prices.
The Senate passed a bill on a 62 to 33 vote Thursday night.
Now goes to the House, which passed a more limited version last year.
The White House has a new national cybersecurity director.
The administration has tapped the Pentagon's chief information officer, Kirsten Davies,
to at least temporarily replace Sean Cairncross after President Trump faced criticism over a cascade of tech outages
that affected air travel, banking, and classified communications.
A hippo that captured global attention after being born prematurely nearly a decade ago has died at the Cincinnati Zoo.
From member station WVXU, Tana Weingartner reports.
Fiona won hearts around the world when she was born six weeks premature at 29 pounds.
Her valiant struggle to survive made her a household name.
A little over a week ago, she ingested a knit hat that was accidentally tossed into her habitat.
The zoo says staff did all they could, but she was unable to pass the object.
They said surgery wasn't an option for a full-size hippo.
In a statement, zoo director Dave Jenneke says they're in shock and didn't expect this outcome.
She fought until she couldn't anymore, he said.
The reaction in Cincinnati and around the country was immediate,
with condolences numbering in the hundreds of thousands in less than an hour after the announcement.
For NPR News, I'm Tana Weingartner in Cincinnati.
And I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump returns to Washington; Franco Ordonez reports on planned White House press conference about Asia trip
Jared Kushner says Russia comfortable with NATO-like security guarantees for post-war Ukraine, in Berlin
Four arrested blocking Anthropic San Francisco offices during protest as Anthropic's record IPO debuts
Senate passes bipartisan bill speeding permitting for power plants and transmission lines, 62-33
Kirsten Davies named White House national cybersecurity director, replacing Sean Cairncross after tech outages
Fiona the hippo dies at Cincinnati Zoo after ingesting a knit hat
